subject: Mud star
topic: This sea star lives in the true abyss, two and a half to three and a half kilometers down.
script:
This sea star lives in the true abyss, two and a half to three and a half kilometers down.
It's a deep-sea mud star.
Mud stars often hide just below the surface of soft mud or sand.
And they have a surprising way of eating.
They swallow whole mouthfuls of sediment, to get at the small snails, clams and other animals living in it.
Scientists often find them with their bodies stuffed full of mud.
This one was spotted out in the open, on the seafloor off western Florida.
It glides along on hundreds of tiny tube feet.
And with its long, pointed arms, it's a surprisingly quick mover for a sea star.
Would you eat mud to find your dinner?
